thread_text:
rachel: quick check — running into a weird funcall schema mismatch between ruby and go SDKs. ruby returns {"foo": null} for missing optional field but go omits the key entirely, and our func-parsing layer treats omitted vs null differently :/

kai: ugh yep. seen that before with streaming func-calls? any repro snippets?

rachel: minimal repro attached inline — ruby client call:
```ruby
client.call_function(name: 'process_item', input: { id: 123 })
# server sees: { "id": 123, "foo": null }
```
and go client:
```go
client.CallFunction(ctx, "process_item", map[string]interface{}{"id":123})
// server sees: {"id":123} // foo missing entirely
```

matt: that will bite typed outputs for sure. our schema parser checks for presence and then coerces types — missing key => skip type check, null => try to coerce which can throw when expecting object/array.

linh: can we standardize on treating missing==null for funccall payloads? or add an SDK helper that normalizes to a canonical shape before sending?

rachel: leaning toward SDK normalization because changing server semantics is riskier for backwards compat. also language SDKs already have different nil vs missing semantics.

kai: +1 for SDK helper. suggestion: add an option/flag `client.normalize_missing_fields = true` which will insert explicit nulls for keys defined in the function schema but missing in the payload. low-risk opt-in.

matt: implementation idea — SDK should fetch the function schema (we already have this for tool discovery) and then run a shallow pass: for each property in schema not present in payload, set value to null when property is not required. Should be easy in ruby/go/py/js.

rachel: caveat: streaming mode — we sometimes send partial payloads or incremental updates; normalization shouldn't break streaming chunks. maybe only normalize on non-streaming calls or at the serializer boundary when assembling final message.

linh: good call. streaming needs minimal changes: only normalize on finalization. also watch out for auth retry flow — we saw a case where a 401 retry re-sent a different shaped payload due to a race between token refresh and normalization.

matt: yeah saw that in CI earlier. ops: devex-bot flagged flaky funccall e2e: `funccall_schema_coercion_test` failing intermittently when token refresh happens mid-serialize.

devex-bot: [automation] Test failure: funccall_schema_coercion_test — last run 1961234540. See logs: https://ci.internal/runs/5321

rachel: proposed plan:
1) add `normalize_missing_fields` opt-in to SDKs (ruby/go/python/js) with default `false`.
2) implement schema fetch + shallow fill on non-streaming calls only.
3) add unit tests + e2e that reproduce the ruby vs go difference.
4) fix the token refresh race by ensuring normalization occurs after token is refreshed (serialize after auth).

kai: sounds reasonable. can we also add a small PR checklist item to document the behavior in the SDK README and the function schema docs?

matt: I'll open a go PR for the helper and a light unit test. link will be in this thread.

matt: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/789 — adds NormalizeMissingFields opt and tests (still WIP). PTAL @rachel @kai

rachel: thanks! I'll mirror in ruby, and linh can handle auth-race tests in e2e harness.

linh: noted, will add a test that simulates token refresh mid-serialize and assert normalization occurs post-refresh.

kai: pinging for reviews: @matt can you add a small changelog entry, and @rachel please add a short code example in the ruby README. then we can graduate the feature to default-on after collecting telemetry for a release cycle.

rachel: will do. also adding a tiny note: server-side we could add a tolerant coercion mode that treats missing==null to help old clients — might open a separate issue after this lands.

matt: agreed. ok moving forward. thanks team :thumbsup:

rachel: tagging this as `needs-cr` and `e2e-needed`. I'll follow up with PR links for the ruby and py SDKs when ready.

kai: awesome. closing the loop here — if anyone hits blockers ping in-thread or DM.
